eventPolicy.costRule: Keep paid events and record cost/registration fields when visible.
eventPolicy.sourceUrlRule: Every event must keep the original event page or source calendar URL.
eventPolicy.qualityRule: Every import must check date coverage, time, place, coordinates, source URL, and activity summary before writing events.json; summaries must contain only useful activity content, not date, time, venue, room, place, or address text; automatically repair deterministic gaps and report anything still missing.
eventPolicy.dateRangeRule: When an event is listed as a date range, expand it so every calendar day in the range is represented unless the source clearly describes one overnight event.
eventPolicy.allDayTimeRule: When an event is listed as all day, check official venue/source hours for that date before filling exact times; if exact hours are not confirmed, leave exact time fields blank where possible and mark timeStatus for review.
eventPolicy.missingAddressRule: When an event gives a venue but no address, search official venue/source pages first, then reliable map or directory sources for the exact street address; if still not found, leave address blank or mark approximate/needs_review rather than guessing.

requiredChecks: date range expansion so every active calendar day has a record or a review marker
startsAt, an exact time, or a clear timeLabel with timeStatus when exact time is unavailable
address when available from the source, official venue page, or reliable address reference
official page text first, then image/flyer text for address, time, room, and venue only when HTML text is incomplete
lat/lng for every in-coverage event shown on the map
summary with concrete activity content only, excluding date, time, venue, room, place, and address text
sourceUrl or url pointing back to the original event page
autoRepair: Copy url and sourceUrl from each other when one is missing.
Copy venue and venueName from each other when one is missing.
Fill timezone from eventPolicy.timezone when startsAt is present.
Calculate durationMinutes from startsAt and endsAt when possible.
Expand multi-day date ranges into per-day event records when the source indicates the event is active across the range.
For all-day rows, fill exact times only from official operating hours for the event date; otherwise preserve a timeLabel and mark timeStatus.
Look up missing venue addresses from official venue/source pages, then reliable map or directory references; do not write guessed addresses.
Use source library/location coordinates first, then town center fallback, then address geocoding for missing in-coverage lat/lng.
Clean generic source-page/update/registration filler and date/time/place/address/venue text out of summaries.
importQuality.unresolvedReportRule: If time, place, coordinates, source URL, or concrete summary are still missing after auto-repair, print an import quality audit with counts and sample event IDs/titles for manual review.
importQuality.contentRule: Do not invent activity descriptions. Extract concrete activity content from the source page when possible; if unavailable, leave summary empty and report it. Put date, time, venue, room, place, and address only in structured fields such as startsAt, endsAt, timeLabel, venueName, venue, and address, never in summary.
importQuality.imageTextRule: Always inspect official page HTML text first. Only when the page text does not provide the needed address, time, room, or venue detail should the importer inspect image alt/title/captions or OCR-visible flyer text; if the importer cannot read the image text, report the event/source for manual image review.
importQuality.uncertaintyRule: If date coverage, time, address, venue, town assignment, or summary is inferred, image-derived, approximate, missing, or uncertain, keep the event useful but mark it with status review, lower confidence, and field-level markers such as dateStatus, dateExpansionStatus, timeStatus, addressStatus, townAssignmentStatus, summaryStatus, or reviewNotes so accuracy-based QA can find it.

sourceStatusVocabulary.importable: Importer should automatically read this source and write events to data/events.json.
sourceStatusVocabulary.manual_review: Source is useful but does not have a stable importer yet; keep the link and parser notes.
sourceStatusVocabulary.service_area: Town is covered by a system source or nearby branch, but there is not a separate branch feed to import.
sourceStatusVocabulary.blocked_by_bot_protection: Source is useful but direct script fetching is blocked; keep it for future browser-backed or manual review.
sourceStatusVocabulary.reference_only: Keep as a directory, venue, or planning reference; do not import events automatically.
sourceStatusVocabulary.not_found: A source type was checked for a town and no useful dated-event source was found.
sourceStatusVocabulary.broken: A previously useful source or parser is currently failing and needs review before import.

appDisplayPolicy.townMenuRule: The More menu displays short town names without Township, Borough, or City suffixes.
appDisplayPolicy.zipRule: Single-ZIP towns show ZIP right-aligned without parentheses; multi-ZIP towns show a parent town row with indented community ZIP rows.
appDisplayPolicy.librarySearchColorRule: Towns with at least one library source marked importable are highlighted in the More menu.
appDisplayPolicy.placeNameRule: Event detail place names may be shortened for display, but source data should keep the original venue name for refresh and review.
appDisplayPolicy.placeDisplayRule: venueName should be a readable venue/place label, not only a street address, intersection, vague downtown area, route, or source placeholder. If the source gives only an address but the registry has a confirmed venue/library name, use the confirmed name for venueName and keep the address in address. If the source gives a place-like display name without a full address, such as a gazebo, bandstand, field, playground, pavilion, plaza, or named room, reverse-look up that display name with the town/venue context and use the resolved address or coordinates for navigation; mark addressLookupSource as place_name_reverse_lookup when practical. If the lookup is likely but not official, keep the useful address, mark addressStatus approximate or needs_review, and preserve the display name in venueName instead of falling back to a generic municipal default. For true street-fair, parade, downtown, route, or multi-site events, keep the broad place label only; use addressStatus area_confirmed when the area/route is confirmed but there is no single precise navigation point, otherwise use addressStatus approximate or needs_review and reviewNotes.
appDisplayPolicy.sourceLinkDisplayRule: When the same activity has multiple source pages, display only one source link in the app. Prefer an official organizer, venue, municipal, library, or program detail page. Use discovery, directory, ticketing, or reposted pages such as Patch or Eventbrite only when no official page is available. Keep extra evidence links internally when helpful for refresh or QA, but the visible button should stay a single Source page.

workflow: Add the town to towns[] with id, name, county, geoid when known, center, distanceMiles, and within-coverage status.
Find and store source links first: municipal/recreation links in towns[].municipal, library links in towns[].libraries[], and reusable or venue-specific links in sharedSources or regionalSources.

Do not stop after government and library sources. For every newly added town, complete the requiredSourceSweep across businesses, museums, arts/science venues, farms/gardens, indoor play venues, malls/retail workshops, downtown/chamber groups, county parks, and other kid-friendly places that may publish dated or limited-time events.
Mark each source with type, status from sourceStatusVocabulary, parser, website, eventsUrl, address/lat/lng when available, and notes about access or parser limits.
Run scripts/import-source-events.mjs to refresh data/events.json from importable sources while keeping older events.
Let the app read data/events.json only; events outside the 30-minute coverage can stay in JSON but should not appear in the app until they are mapped to coverage.

requiredSourceSweep.rule: Every town expansion must search beyond municipal and public-library calendars. Treat all places where children can play, learn, watch, build, craft, read, explore, or attend seasonal programs as potential event sources.
requiredSourceSweep.scope: Search sources physically in the new town plus nearby venues that serve the town or sit inside the active drive-time coverage area. Prefer official venue pages, official calendars, booking pages, and stable APIs before third-party aggregators.
minimumChecklist: Municipal calendar, parks/recreation department, recreation registration portal, municipal alliance, school/community supplement pages, and official news/flyer pages.
Public library branch calendars, county library system feeds, nearby service-area branches, and youth/teen/family pages.
Downtown/SID/chamber/business association calendars, street fairs, farmers markets, and local business district pages.
County parks, nature centers, environmental education centers, gardens, arboretums, farms, wildlife centers, zoos, and seasonal outdoor venues.
Museums, science centers, art centers, historic sites, theaters, music venues, maker spaces, and cultural centers with family or youth programs.
Indoor playgrounds, trampoline parks, sensory gyms, kids gyms, sports complexes, swim schools, dance/martial arts studios, STEM/coding centers, party venues, and camp/class providers.
Malls, shopping centers, bookstores, toy/game stores, LEGO/Apple-style retail programs, craft stores, home-improvement kids workshops, and restaurants/cafes that host family events.
Regional festival, carnival, fair, market, and tourism directories that can be mapped back to covered towns.
requiredSourceSweep.recordingRule: Record every useful source even when it is not importable yet. Use importable when an importer can read it, manual_review when it needs human/browser review, service_area when covered by a broader system, blocked_by_bot_protection when direct fetching is blocked, and reference_only only for directories or venues without dated event potential.
requiredSourceSweep.stopRule: A new town source update is incomplete until each checklist category has either an importable/manual source entry or a note explaining why no useful dated-event source was found.

configuredEvents.title: Four Centuries in a Weekend
configuredEvents.summary: (all ages) Four Centuries in a Weekend is a Union County tradition that enables residents and visitors to travel through time and learn about the rich history of our community. Reeves-Reed Arboretum is participating on Saturday, October 17 from 10 am – 4 pm. We will be offering the following activities that will help you learn about the history of this historic estate now known as Reeves-Reed Arboretum: Visit our history exhibit to view artifacts and photographs of the Reeves, Reed, and Wisner families. Take a free Horticulture & History Tour at 10:30 am or 1:30 pm (meet at the Visitors Center). Grab a Map & Guide from our Visitors Center to aide your self-guided tour throughout the grounds, trails and gardens. Our new ADA accessible pathway (‘A Path for All’) is now open, linking all garden areas. Stop by Beacon Signal Fire #10, a replica of the original Revolutionary War beacon on “the hill”. Walk along the Wildflower Trail and stop to read our interpretive signage highlighting the property’s history. Visit the current art exhibit in historic Wisner House. This is a free Union County event. No registration is required. For more information about Union County’s Four Centuries in a Weekend, click here .

configuredEvents.title: Free Saturday Tours
configuredEvents.summary: (all ages) Enjoy a Free Guided Tour of the Arboretum Free guided tours of the Arboretum are offered most Saturdays at 10:30 am and 1:30 pm, from April 18 through October 17. Tours begin at the Visitors Center. No reservations are required and tours are on a first-come, first-served basis for individuals who would like to learn more about the current season’s highlights. Limit of 7 people per tour. Anyone under the age of 12 must be accompanied by an adult. No groups. Tours last approximately 30-45 minutes. Saturday Garden Tours may be suspended on days with excessive heat. Please check the website for updated hours. We apologize for any inconvenience.

configuredEvents.title: Celebrate Fall Festival 2026
configuredEvents.summary: Join Us for Celebrate Fall! Get ready to fall in love with the season at our Celebrate Fall Festival! With Halloween just around the corner, there’s something for everyone—whether you’re crafting, playing games, or simply enjoying the crisp autumn air. Wander through our Spooky Trail if you dare, and immerse yourself in the vibrant colors of our garden as it transforms into a golden autumn paradise. Let the kids enjoy fun games, crafts, and of course, meet our adorable goats. Plus, don’t forget to stop by our market vendors for some delicious seasonal treats! It’s the perfect way to celebrate fall with family and friends!! Member (& Children under 3) Price: $0 | Non-Member Price: $15 Celebrate Fall is FREE for RRA members. Registration for Family Level members is limited to immediate family only. Individual and Senior Level members are entitled to one entry, while Dual Level members are entitled to two entries. Celebrate Fall is FREE for children under 3. When registering, please indicate the number of people attending. ARRIVAL: Please consider carpooling, walking, or biking to the Arboretum if possible. We are in a residential neighborhood, and parking will be available only on the street. Our parking lot is closed for this event to accommodate vendors. Please be courteous to our neighbors by not blocking driveways and obeying all parking signs. Walk to our entry gate to check in. Bikes can be stored in our bicycle racks. QUESTIONS? Please email info@reeves-reedarboretum.org ; Sponsorship Opportunities – Contact k.cerf@reeves-reedarboretum.org. Thank you to our sponsor, Lees Group, our in-kind sponsors, Lorenz Fine Photography and ShopRite.

configuredEvents.title: Beginner Modern Calligraphy Workshop
configuredEvents.summary: (adults and teens 14 yrs+) Introducing the Elegant Basics of Modern Calligraphy, where you’ll explore a new skill in a relaxed and enjoyable class. Grounded in traditional ink and nib techniques, you’ll learn how to use an oblique pen and develop a strong foundation in pointed pen calligraphy. Through live demonstrations and guided practice, you’ll master essential calligraphy strokes designed to help you build confidence and skill. You’ll learn to write minuscules, be introduced to majuscules, and connect letters to create your own words and phrases. Your beginner pointed pen calligraphy kit has been specially curated to support your practice with professional-quality tools. You’ll take home beginner-friendly nibs, a packet of time-tested paper samples, an exemplars packet, and a clear instructional booklet to encourage continued practice at home. configuredEvents.title: Encaustic Art Demonstration with Pascale Bouchard
configuredEvents.summary: (adults and teens 16 yrs+) Join exhibiting artist Pascale Bouchard for an intimate, interactive demonstration of the encaustic techniques behind her work in Féminin Pluriel. During this approximately 1½-hour presentation, Pascale will introduce participants to the history of encaustic, the materials and tools she uses, and the many ways this ancient medium can be transformed with heat, wax, pigment, texture, and layering. Through a live demonstration, she will share techniques including working and layering wax, image transfers, incorporating paper, photographs, thread and other materials, creating texture and transparency, and using heated tools, brushes, torches and a heat gun to manipulate the wax. This is an interactive artist demonstration rather than a hands-on workshop, so participants will be seated and can ask questions throughout the presentation. Following the demonstration, Pascale will be available for informal conversation and participants will have the opportunity to walk through the Féminin Pluriel exhibit with the artist and hear more about the techniques, stories, and inspiration behind individual works. Whether you are familiar with encaustic or simply curious about how these richly textured works are created, this is a unique opportunity to learn directly from the artist and take a closer look at her creative process. Please note: This event does not include a hands-on art-making component. Féminin Pluriel is a solo exhibition by Québec-based artist Pascale Bouchard featuring her distinctive encaustic work inspired by floral imagery, organic forms, transformation and the symbolic power of the feminine. This event is FREE to attend, but registration is required. A suggested donation of $10 helps support Reeves-Reed Arboretum and its ongoing art exhibits and programs. Donate here.

configuredEvents.title: Meet the Artist & Closing Reception: Pascale Bouchard in Action
configuredEvents.summary: (adults and teens 16 yrs+) Join us for an afternoon with artist Pascale Bouchard as we celebrate the closing of her exhibition, Féminin Pluriel . Enjoy refreshments while meeting Pascale and getting a firsthand look at her encaustic process. Pascale will be working with encaustic in the gallery, giving visitors the opportunity to watch her create, ask questions, and see the materials and tools she uses up close. You’ll be able to discover the textures, layers, wax, pigments and other materials that come together in her work and gain a better understanding of the process behind the pieces on display. Take your time exploring Féminin Pluriel , meet the artist, and enjoy an informal afternoon of art, conversation and refreshments. Féminin Pluriel is a solo exhibition by Québec-based artist Pascale Bouchard featuring her distinctive encaustic work inspired by floral imagery, organic forms, transformation and the symbolic power of the feminine. This event is FREE to attend, but registration is suggested so we can plan accordingly.

configuredEvents.title: Beginner Modern Calligraphy Workshop
configuredEvents.summary: (adults and teens 14 yrs+) Discover the elegant basics of modern calligraphy in this relaxed and fun class. Grounded in the traditional use of ink and nib, you’ll learn how to use an oblique pen and practice key calligraphy strokes demonstrated live to help you build confidence and skill. With practice, you’ll learn to write minuscules, be introduced to majuscules, and connect letters to create your own words. You’ll also take home a beginner’s pointed-pen calligraphy kit, specially curated to support continued practice with professional-quality tools. The kit includes beginner-friendly nibs, a packet of time-tested paper samples, an exemplars packet, and an instruction booklet to guide your at-home practice. configuredEvents.title: Sponsor & Decorate a Tree for our Holiday Open House!
configuredEvents.summary: (children & adults) Calling local businesses, organizations, families, schools, and scout groups! Sponsor a tree, bring your creativity, and help us fill Reeves-Reed Arboretum with holiday cheer! Decorated trees will be featured at our Holiday Open House, where visitors can vote for their favorites. On Sunday, December 6, 2026, we will be holding our annual Holiday Open House , and we invite YOU to help make it a success! STEP 1: Sign up to sponsor and decorate a tree! RRA will provide and set up the trees, you just need the decorations. The deadline to register is December 1. We will have a limited number of trees, so don’t wait to sign up. STEP 2: Decorate! Gather your family, friends, or colleagues and come to the Arboretum on Saturday, December 5, 10 am – 2 pm to create your display. Be creative, there will be prizes! STEP 3: Return on Sunday, December 6 with your two complimentary tickets for the Holiday Open House to enjoy the fun! Sip ‘n Shop at our Holiday Market for unique gifts, holiday décor, delicious treats, and more! Explore the Winter Story Walk, Candy Cane Lane, and make a Winter Craft. Enjoy Live Holiday Carolers and of course touring the trees and voting for your favorite one! Tickets for the Holiday Open House are $10 for adults, children under 12 are free. STEP 4: After the event, you are welcome to take your tree home or remove the decorations and leave it on the Arboretum grounds. We can use the trees to make mulch or use the branches to protect our beds from frost during the winter months. Details in FAQ below. Answers to frequently asked questions: Trees are approximately 5-6 feet tall and are in stands. If you choose to string lights, please make sure they are battery operated since electricity is not available on the grounds. It is recommended that ornaments be able to withstand rain/snow and are secure in case of windy conditions. Balloons and candles are not permitted. Additional items/props can be placed under or near your tree. Get creative! Some previous themes have included: Wordle, Goats, Sports, Cooking, etc. Each tree will have an assigned number, the title of your tree, and the name of your group/business. You will receive further details about the decorating sessions via email a few days before 12/5 . First and second place prizes will be awarded. Winners will be notified within a day or two of the event, and we will post the winning trees on social media. If you are taking your tree home after the event on Sunday, it can be removed from the stand and taken between 4 – 4:30 pm. If you are coming back for the tree, please remove it by 4 pm Wednesday 12/9. If you are not keeping the tree, all decorations, props, etc. must be removed after the event ends between 4 – 4:30 pm or by 4 pm Wednesday 12/9. SPONSOR PRICING: Nonprofits/Families/School and Scout Groups $125; Corporate/Businesses $150 IMPORTANT: Please indicate in the details box on the check-out page that this donation is for Sponsoring a Festival Tree . Please also indicate the name of your group/family/business/organization. Click here to pay your sponsor fee. Need additional tickets for the event? Click here. Tickets will also be available at the door for purchase. Thank you for supporting our non-profit public gardens, grounds, and environmental education programs! HAVE ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS? Please contact Jackie Kondel at j.kondel@reeves-reedarboretum.org .

configuredEvents.title: Beginner Ornament Lettering Workshop
configuredEvents.summary: (adults and teens 14 yrs+) Discover the elegant basics of marker calligraphy lettering while exploring a new skill in a relaxed and fun class. Learn how to use a bullet-tip marker to create beautiful calligraphy lettering on a variety of surfaces. configuredEvents.title: The Sky Above
configuredEvents.summary: This sensory-friendly astronomy and music show, approximately 45 minutes in length, is specially designed for families with children on the Autism spectrum or those with developmental disabilities. Neurotypical children are welcome as well. The program, which is presented on a kindergarten level, is appropriate for audiences of all ages. During the show, the doors will remain open so children may freely leave and return if they choose. Lights will be left dim (instead of dark), and the audio will be lowered and kept at a consistent level. The show will include music, laser lights, stories, and information about the planets, the Moon and constellations.

configuredEvents.title: Revolutionary Skies
configuredEvents.summary: Did the sky play a part in the Revolutionary War? Did the Moon guide a nighttime informant? Who crossed into enemy territory “in the name of science?” Learn about celestial events and scientists during the Revolutionary War period.

configuredEvents.title: Redcoats to Rebels laser concert
configuredEvents.summary: The British are coming…and bringing rockin’ music! Enjoy rock ‘n’ roll songs popular during the famous “British Invasion.” Bands include The Who, Led Zeppelin, and Queen. Then we’ll switch continents and enjoy some classic rock songs from American bands like Journey, Guns N Roses, Bon Jovi, Twisted Sister, and more.

configuredEvents.title: Rooted at Duke Farms
configuredEvents.summary: Join Duke Farms for an intimate evening of connection: between you, your meal, and the living systems that make it possible. At Duke Farms, we believe food systems are conservation systems . What we grow, how we grow it, where food comes from, and the relationships that bring it to our tables are all connected to the health of our soil, water, habitats, farms, and communities. As Executive Chef and Culinary Program Lead at Duke Farms, Chef Lauren Owens approaches food as a way to connect people to place. Her work is rooted in seasonality, regional agriculture, thoughtful sourcing, and hospitality, using the table to bring the larger story of our food system into focus. Throughout the evening, Chef Lauren’s seasonal menu will become a doorway into that larger story. You’ll meet some of the people behind the ingredients and hear brief stories from staff and partners. Together, they’ll trace a meal back to the land that sustains it. This is also an invitation to become part of what happens here. Duke Farms is a living laboratory where conservation is tested, shared, and experienced in real time. By gathering at this table, you are joining a community that believes people and nature can work together to shape better solutions. This is not a dinner beside our mission. It is a seat within it. Agenda Cocktail Hour Curated cocktails and hors d’oeuvres, and a warm welcome from our Executive Director. Dinner A meal prepared with seasonal, locally-sourced ingredients, paired with moments of micro-storytelling. Dessert Delectable delights and a sweet send-off. Why Duke Farms? A dinner about food systems is one of the clearest ways to experience conservation up close. The health of a meal begins before it reaches the kitchen: in soil, water, biodiversity, growing practices, and the choices that connect producers with communities. Across Duke Farms, those relationships are part of our work every day, from agroecology and stewardship to public learning and partnerships with regional growers. Rooted brings those to the table. It is a chance to experience Duke Farms not only as a place to visit, but as a place where ideas about conservation are put into practice and where our community can be part of what comes next. About the Chef Chef Lauren Owens is the Executive Chef and Culinary Program Lead at Duke Farms, where she connects food, farming, and environmental stewardship through culinary experiences. Her career spans kitchens, classrooms, and entrepreneurship, including roles at Hilton Short Hills, Blue Hill, and Harvest Restaurant Group, where she served as Executive Chef of Urban Table in Morristown. She is the founder of Tiny Onion Chef Services and is passionate about mentoring the next generation, expanding access in culinary and food systems spaces, and using food as a tool for education, opportunity, and community impact.

configuredEvents.title: LGBTQ+ Book Discussion: Shuggie Bain, by Douglas Stuart
configuredEvents.summary: The Newark Public Library LGBTQ+ Resource Center presents a monthly book discussion group, where all backgrounds and identities are welcome and encouraged to participate. Join us at the Main Library, LGBTQ+ Resource Center, Wednesday, October 21 from 6PM - 8PM for a group discussion of Shuggie Bain, by Douglas Stuart. Shuggie Bain is the unforgettable story of young Hugh “Shuggie” Bain, a sweet and lonely boy who spends his 1980s childhood in run-down public housing in Glasgow, Scotland. Thatcher’s policies have put husbands and sons out of work, and the city’s notorious drugs epidemic is waiting in the wings. Shuggie’s mother Agnes walks a wayward path: she is Shuggie’s guiding light but a burden for him and his siblings. She dreams of a house with its own front door while she flicks through the pages of the Freemans catalogue, ordering a little happiness on credit, anything to brighten up her grey life. Married to a philandering taxi-driver husband, Agnes keeps her pride by looking good―her beehive, make-up, and pearly-white false teeth offer a glamourous image of a Glaswegian Elizabeth Taylor. But under the surface, Agnes finds increasing solace in drink, and she drains away the lion’s share of each week’s benefits―all the family has to live on―on cans of extra-strong lager hidden in handbags and poured into tea mugs. Agnes’s older children find their own ways to get a safe distance from their mother, abandoning Shuggie to care for her as she swings between alcoholic binges and sobriety. Shuggie is meanwhile struggling to somehow become the normal boy he desperately longs to be, but everyone has realized that he is “no right,” a boy with a secret that all but him can see. Agnes is supportive of her son, but her addiction has the power to eclipse everyone close to her―even her beloved Shuggie. A heartbreaking story of addiction, sexuality, and love, Shuggie Bain is an epic portrayal of a working-class family that is rarely seen in fiction. Recalling the work of Édouard Louis, Alan Hollinghurst, Frank McCourt, and Hanya Yanagihara, it is a blistering debut by a brilliant novelist who has a powerful and important story to tell. Registration is required and linked below. Free copies of the book are available and will be provided upon request*. *Please note that free copies of the book are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, and will only be distributed to those who commit to attending the discussion.

configuredEvents.title: Meet & Make
configuredEvents.summary: Formerly known as Meet & Mend, Meet & Make is our monthly hand-sewing class. Jump into a guided hand-sewing project, learn new skills, and be in community. Now with a new instructor, Mark Menzie , who brings hands-on guidance, real industry experience, and a welcoming approach to learning how to sew and mend with confidence. ABOUT MARK MENZIE Mark E. Menzie is a Newark-based fashion designer, stylist, and educator with over a decade of experience in the fashion industry. He is the founder and creative director of Menzie by Design , a youth-focused fashion and lifestyle brand centered on creativity, craftsmanship, and self-expression. A graduate of the Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), Mark has studied fashion design, trend forecasting in France and Italy, and fashion business and entrepreneurship. His professional background spans luxury retail, styling, product development, and community-based arts education. As an instructor, Mark is passionate about making fashion accessible and culturally relevant for young people. His classes blend traditional sewing skills with hands-on crafts, storytelling, and design history—often drawing inspiration from childhood techniques like paper dolls, patchwork, and upcycling. Through his teaching, he empowers students to build confidence, creativity, and practical skills while seeing themselves reflected in the world of fashion and design. ABOUT MADE@NPL Made@NPL is a community resource located at Newark Public Library's Main Branch that provides all Newarkers access to in-demand equipment, technology, and software, to use at no cost. Made@NPL supports creative entrepreneurs with business reference services and programming related to creativity, entrepreneurship, and making things. Made@NPL was funded by a generous grant from the PNC Foundation.

Instructor Joni Wellness, a yoga teacher with decades of experience, will present classical yoga taught safely in progressive increments, within each class and from class to class, that build knowledge and safe practice according to one’s abilities. Students are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and other yoga props if they have them. The library has a small number of yoga mats for use. Classes will be in the auditorium on the 4th floor of Main Library. Registration is strongly encouraged. Mat Yoga class provides an opportunity for experiential learning of classical yoga philosophy (e.g., non-violence, tolerance, self-study) through exploration of yoga postures. Detailed instruction with component breakdown of postures supporting strength, mobility, mindfulness, self-study, stress reduction, healing and transformation. Fall 2026 Mat Yoga Tuesdays, 5 pm - 6:30 pm September 29; October 6, 13, 20, 27; November 10, 17, 24; December 1, 8 (no class November 3--library closed)

configuredEvents.title: LGBTQ+ Book Discussion: These Heathens, by Mia McKenzie
configuredEvents.summary: The Newark Public Library LGBTQ+ Resource Center presents a monthly book discussion group, where all backgrounds and identities are welcome and encouraged to participate. Join us at the Main Library, LGBTQ+ Resource Center, Wednesday, November 18 from 6PM - 8PM for a group discussion of These Heathens , by Mia McKenzie From the “razor-sharp and outrageously funny” (Taylor Jenkins Reid) mind of Mia McKenzie comes a vibrant novel exploring how one weekend can change your whole life. FINALIST FOR THE LOS ANGELES TIMES BOOK PRIZE • LONGLISTED FOR THE ANDREW CARNEGIE MEDAL AND THE ASPEN WORDS LITERARY PRIZE • A CHICAGO PUBLIC LIBRARY BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR Dear Lord, please forgive me for the sins I’ve committed. And for the one I’m still planning to commit tomorrow. Amen. Where do you get an abortion in 1960 Georgia, especially if your small town’s midwife goes to the same church as your parents? For 17-year-old Doris Steele, the answer is Atlanta, where her favorite teacher, Mrs. Lucas, calls upon her brash, wealthy childhood best friend, Sylvia, for help. While waiting to hear from the doctor who has agreed to do the procedure, Doris spends the weekend scandalized by, but drawn to, the people who move in and out of Sylvia’s orbit: celebrities whom Doris has seen in the pages of Jet and Ebony, civil rights leaders such as Coretta Scott King and Diane Nash, women who dance close together, boys who flirt too hard and talk too much, atheists! And even more shocking? Mrs. Lucas seems right at home. From the guests at a queer kickback to the student activists at a SNCC conference, Doris suddenly finds herself surrounded by so many people who seem to know exactly who or what they want. Doris knows she doesn’t want a baby, but what does she want? Will this trip help her find out? These Heathens is a funny, poignant story about Black women’s obligations and ambitions, what we owe to ourselves, and the transformative power of leaving your bubble, even for just one chaotic weekend. Registration is required and linked below. Free copies of the book are available and will be provided upon request*. *Please note that free copies of the book are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, and will only be distributed to those who commit to attending the discussion.

configuredEvents.title: Overdose Prevention / Narcan Training: "I Want to See You Live" with Newark Community Street Team Overdose Response Team
configuredEvents.summary: All over the city of Newark there are overdoses--fatal and non-fatal--on a daily basis. The Newark Community Street Team - Overdose Response Team (NCST-ORT) is out in the field and knows what's going on. The key to preventing overdoses and deaths, the key to " seeing people live " is Narcan/Naloxone education and training. The importance of both having access to Narcan and knowing what to do in response to an Overdose is crucial . Participants will learn about the importance of naloxone in preventing overdose deaths and how to administer it in an emergency. This event is for all who consider themselves human. Please join us for this essential workshop. Registration is encouraged but not required. Tuesday, January 20, 2025 @ 11 am Wednesday, March 18, 2025 @ 11 am Thursday, May 14, 2025 @ 11 am Monday, July 13, 2025 @ 11 am Tuesday, September 22, 2025 @ 11 am Thursday, November 19, 2025 @ 11 am Auditorium, 4th Floor Newark Main Library 5 Washington St.

Instructor Joni Wellness, a yoga teacher with decades of experience, will present classical yoga taught safely in progressive increments, within each class and from class to class, that build knowledge and safe practice according to one’s abilities. Students are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and other yoga props if they have them. The library has a small number of yoga mats for use. Classes will be in the auditorium on the 4th floor of Main Library. Registration is strongly encouraged. Mat Yoga class provides an opportunity for experiential learning of classical yoga philosophy (e.g., non-violence, tolerance, self-study) through exploration of yoga postures. Detailed instruction with component breakdown of postures supporting strength, mobility, mindfulness, self-study, stress reduction, healing and transformation. Fall 2026 Mat Yoga Tuesdays, 5 pm - 6:30 pm September 29; October 6, 13, 20, 27; November 10, 17, 24; December 1, 8 (no class November 3--library closed)

configuredEvents.title: Audio Club: Album Recording Sessions
configuredEvents.summary: Join Audio Club, a songwriting session where musicians, singers, producers, rappers, songwriters, engineers, and creatives come together to create original music. Whether you're bringing a finished idea, a rough demo, or starting from scratch, Audio Club is built around collaboration. Work with a team of artists, write songs, record vocals and instruments, produce beats, exchange feedback, and help bring each other's ideas to life in the Made@NPL Audio Booth. Throughout the season, participants will collaborate on original tracks with the opportunity to be featured on Audio Club Volume 2, our community-produced compilation album celebrating Newark's creative talent. Audio Club meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of every month from 5:30–7:30 PM. Come build your network, sharpen your skills, and be part of a collaborative album from concept to release.

configuredEvents.title: Meet & Make
configuredEvents.summary: Formerly known as Meet & Mend, Meet & Make is our monthly hand-sewing class. Jump into a guided hand-sewing project, learn new skills, and be in community. Now with a new instructor, Mark Menzie , who brings hands-on guidance, real industry experience, and a welcoming approach to learning how to sew and mend with confidence. ABOUT MARK MENZIE Mark E. Menzie is a Newark-based fashion designer, stylist, and educator with over a decade of experience in the fashion industry. He is the founder and creative director of Menzie by Design , a youth-focused fashion and lifestyle brand centered on creativity, craftsmanship, and self-expression. A graduate of the Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), Mark has studied fashion design, trend forecasting in France and Italy, and fashion business and entrepreneurship. His professional background spans luxury retail, styling, product development, and community-based arts education. As an instructor, Mark is passionate about making fashion accessible and culturally relevant for young people. His classes blend traditional sewing skills with hands-on crafts, storytelling, and design history—often drawing inspiration from childhood techniques like paper dolls, patchwork, and upcycling. Through his teaching, he empowers students to build confidence, creativity, and practical skills while seeing themselves reflected in the world of fashion and design. ABOUT MADE@NPL Made@NPL is a community resource located at Newark Public Library's Main Branch that provides all Newarkers access to in-demand equipment, technology, and software, to use at no cost. Made@NPL supports creative entrepreneurs with business reference services and programming related to creativity, entrepreneurship, and making things. Made@NPL was funded by a generous grant from the PNC Foundation.
